title: dataStructure.yml: attributes on abstract classes carry a subclass's C-code, preferred term and definition (27 attributes)
body:
For attributes on abstract classes, `dataStructure.yml` and `USDM_CT.xlsx` give different C-codes. In all 27 cases where they differ, the YAML carries the code, preferred term and definition of one concrete subclass, while `USDM_CT.xlsx` has its own entry for the abstract class attribute.

Example, `SyntaxTemplate.text` (inherited by Characteristic, Condition, EligibilityCriterionItem, Endpoint, IntercurrentEvent and Objective):

- `USDM_CT.xlsx` row 285: C207578 Syntax Template Text, "A structured text string containing prescribed text interspersed with user-defined parameter values."
- `dataStructure.yml`: C207478 Characteristic Text, "An instance of structured text that represents the characteristic." This is the `USDM_CT.xlsx` entry for Characteristic.text (row 393).

This looks like a side effect of the generator choice described in #525: "the attributes shown for them are the inherited attributes from the first sub class listed". That fixed the Id / Ids references, but the C-code, preferred term and definition come from the subclass too. A consumer reading the YAML gets, for the text of an Objective, a definition about "the characteristic".

Ask: for attributes on abstract classes, take the C-code, preferred term and definition from the abstract class's own `USDM_CT.xlsx` entry (abstract classes were kept in CT, see #196), or state in the documentation of `dataStructure.yml` that these entries mirror the first subclass.
